segments.en: And therefore one who makes his entire dough into Chalah has done nothing, as it is said: “raishis” [firstfruits] — meaning that its remainder (shirayim) must be recognizable — as is explained in the Shulchan Aruch. For this is the essential rectification: that through the raishis [first portion] which one separates, the shirayim [remainder] too are rectified and ascend to holiness, in the aspect of “v'nish'ar gam hu le'Elokaynu” [and he shall remain also to our G-d]. “V'nish'ar” [and he shall remain] specifically — meaning that the aspect of the shirayim, the aspect of “v'nish'ar gam hu le'Elokaynu,” it too shall ascend to Hashem blessed-be-He, to its supernal root. And this is the essential wholeness of Creation — which was created for this: that the shirayim too should ascend to holiness through the raishis, which is the essential thing for whose sake everything was created, as it is written: “Beraishis bara Elokim” [In the beginning G-d created] etc. (Beraishis 1:1). And our Sages of blessed memory expounded: “for the sake of Israel who are called the firstfruits of His produce, and for the sake of the Torah which is called the beginning of His way” etc. (Rashi, Beraishis 1:1). It turns out that Israel and the Torah are the essential raishis for whose sake everything was created — the heavens and the earth and all that is in them. And therefore certainly the heavens and the earth etc. — all of them are called shirayim in relation to the Torah and Israel who are the raishis.

segments.he: כי כל הדברים קודם שאוכלם ונהנה מהם צריך להגביהם להם חיות מן הקדושה ואז המאכל ראוי לאכילת ישרלאת. כי מקודם היה לו חיות מבחי' עץ הדעת שעל ידו נפלו כל הדברים בין הקליפות. וע"כ צריך לברך קודם כל דבר שרוצים ליהנות ממנו. כי ע"י הברכה שמברכין ומודים להש"י שברא אותו הדבר. עי"ז מעלין אותו הדגבר ומרימין אותו למעלה לשרשו שבקדושה וממשיכין לו חיות משם כי ע" יהדיבור של הברכה שואמרין למשל בורא פרי העץ. עי"ז כאלו נברא הדבר מחדש כי עתה נתתקן ונמשך לו חיות מן הקדושה ונמצא שבוראו עתה מחדש ממש. וכמובא לעיל בה' נדרים (הלכה א'):
segments.en: And the essential rectification is when one knows who is the raishis and who is the shirayim. And all the world and its fullness which are the shirayim — when they toil on their behalf (torchim bisvilam), then the shirayim too are rectified through the raishis, and then everything returns to Hashem blessed-be-He in the aspect of “v'nish'ar gam hu le'Elokaynu” — as will be in the future. But as long as one does not separate the raishis and does not know who is the raishis and who is the shirayim — and all the more so when, heaven forbid, one inverts the truth and makes the tail into a head etc. — then the whole world is disordered, heaven forbid. And this is the aspect of “and the earth was” etc. (Beraishis 1:2) — for at the beginning of Creation, which was for the sake of the raishis so that through it the shirayim might be rectified as mentioned — but then, at the start, who was the raishis had not yet been revealed and was not recognizable. For the holiness of Israel and the Torah, which are the raishis, had not yet been revealed. And therefore it was then said: “and the earth was tohu vavohu [formless and void] and darkness” etc. (ibid.) — for as long as the raishis is not revealed, the whole world is disordered in the aspect of tohu vavohu and darkness etc. — as now in the exile, when Israel who are the raishis are subdued in exile and they [the nations] are at the head etc. And this is what the Midrash expounded: tohu vavohu and darkness refer to the exiles of the four kingdoms — as they said there: “tohu — this is the kingdom of Babylon” etc., “vavohu” etc. That is: tohu vavohu etc. alludes to the time of the exiles when Israel are subdued in exile and the raishis — for whose sake everything was created — is not recognizable. But the essential sustenance in the exile is through the aspect of “and the spirit of G-d” — da rucho shel Mashiach [this is the spirit of Mashiach] — “hovered over the face of the waters” — da Orayta [this is the Torah] (Zohar, Beraishis 2a) — for Mashiach is destined to redeem us speedily, and he also sustains and preserves us throughout all the days of the exile through the Torah that illuminates in us and informs us that Hashem is still with us, and that we should not despair of Him blessed-be-He. For we still have hope — every single one of us, in general and in particular. And through this: “and G-d said: let there be light, and there was light” (Beraishis 1:3) — for through this Hashem blessed-be-He illuminates for us at every moment, until we merit to discern who is the raishis and who is the shirayim.

segments.he: וזה בחי' תרומה ומעשר. ומעשר מן המעשר שהוא ג"כ תרומה. ולכאורה הדבר תמוה מאחר שמצוה להפריש עוד תרומה שניה. דהיינו מעשר מן המעשר הי' ראוי להפריש הכל בבת אחת. כי הלא אין שום הפרש וחילוק בין התרומה ראשונה לאחרונה כי שניהם לכהן ושניהם קדושים בקדושה אחת כדין תרומה. אך ע"פ מה דאיתא בדברי רבינו נ"י במאמר ויהי נא פי שנים (בסי' ס"ו) שיש ב' רוחו רוח לעילא ורוח לתתא ובתחילה שניה םאחד ואז הוא בחי' קודם הבריאה ואח"כ צריך להוציא מכח אל הפועל ואזי נתחלקים לבחי' ב' הרוחות הנ"ל. ולהוציא מכח אל הפועל הוא ע"י הדיבור וכו' ע"ש. וזה בחי' תרומה לכהן ומעשר ללוי. ומעשר מן המעשר שהוא תרומה שניה ג"כ לכהן. כי תרומה הראשונה אין לה שיעור כיהיא בבחי' רוח דלעילא שהוא בבחי' חכמה. כי כולם בחכמה עשית כי הוא בחי' יו"ד ראשונה שהוא בחי' מחשבה שבמוח היינו בחי' חכמה שהוא נקרא קודש. וע"כ אין לה שיעור כי שם בתחלת המשחבה שהוא בחי' כח בחי' רוח דלעילא הנ"ל עדיין אין שם שיעור ומדה כלל. רק היא נטלת מאומד ומחשבה כי היא בבחי' מחשבה שבמוח בחי' כח כנ"ל. כי כל המדות והשיעורים הם רק אחר הבריאה והרוח דלעילא הוא בבחי' קודם הבראיה כנ"ל. והתרומה שניה שהיא מעשר מן המעשר היא בחי' רוח דלתתא שהוא בחי' פועל ששם המדות והשיעורין. וע"כ היא מעשר מן המעשר כי החיות דלתתא הוא רק חלק ממאה בחי' מעשר מן המעשר. בסוד חייב אדם לברך מאה ברכות בכל יום כמובא. וע"כ צריכין להפריש מקודם המעשר. כי המעשר הואבחי' מלכות פה בחי' הדיבור שהוא בחי' מעשר מן המחשבה מבחי' רוח דלעילא והוא ניתן ללוי שהוא בבחי' הדיבור בבחי' וגבורתך ידברו שהוא סטרא דלוי כידוע. שהלוים הם בבחי' גבורות וע"י הדיבור מוציאין מכח אל הפועל. דהיינו ע,שי המעשר ללוי שהוא בחי' דיבור עי"ז מוציאין מכח אל הפועל ואזי נמשך הרוח דלתתא שהוא בבחי' פועל. וזה בחי' מעשר מן המעשר שהוא ג"כ תרומה שהוא בחי' רוח דללתא כנ"ל. וכן מרומז ג"כ בדברי רבינו במ"א (בסי' נ"א) שהלוי היא בחי' הממוצע בין קודם הבריאה לאחר הבריאה כמובא במאמר אר"ע כשתגיע לאבני ששי טהור וכו' ע"ש. וע"כ נקרא בשם לוי לשון התחברות כ"ש הפעם ילוה אישי אלי היינו שהוא בחי' הדיבור המחבר רוח דלעילא ורוח דלתתא. כי הוא ממוצע בין שניהם וכלול משניהם וכמובא בדברי רבינו נ"י (בסי' י"א) שהדיבגור נקרא ציפרתא דקאי וכו' דרישי' מטי עד צית שמיא וקרסולי' במיא למטה כי הדיבור כלול מלמעלה ומלמטה. כי הוא מוציא מכח אל הפועל ששזה עקיר הבריאה כ"ש שם. וע"כ נקרא הדיגור הקדוש של בחי' לה"ק פי שנים. כ"ש רבינו (בסי' י"ט) בבחי' ויהי נא פי שנים ברוחך כ"ש שם כי הוא פי שנים ממש כי כלול משני הרוחות הנ"ל כנ"ל. וע"כ נתנו חכמים שיעור לתרומה ראשונה תרי ממאה כי הרוח דלעילא כלול מב' הרוחות כי זהכלל שהעליון כלול מהתחתון כי ההשתלשלות מראשית מהחשבה שהוא בחינת רוח דלעילא עד סוף המעשה שהוא הרוח דלתתא הוא עד בחי' מאה בבחי' א"ת מה אלא מאה שזה בחי' מאה ברכות כנ"ל שזה בחי' מעשר מן המעשר שהוא חלק ממאה כנ"ל. וע"כ הרוח דלעילא שהוא כלול מב' הרוחות הוא פי שנים כתחתון היינו תרי ממאה כי הוא כלול משניהם כנ"ל. ובאמת מעיקר הדין מדאורייתא אין לתרומה ראשונה שום שיעור כי שם למעלה מן השיעור והמדמה כנ"ל. רק חכמים נתנו לו שיעור ע"ש סופו. כי סופו להשתלשל עד למטה עד סוף המעשה. כי סוף מעשה במחשבה תחלה כמובא שם במאמר ויהי נא פי שנים הנ"ל ע"ש וע"כ שני התרומות לכהן. כי הכהן הוא בבחי' חכמה כמובא שמשם הוא בחי' ב' הרוחות בבחי' כולם בחכמה עשית. וע"י אלו המתנות הנ"ל. עי"ז מרימין ומעלין התבואה ומתקניןאותה כאו בוראין אותה מחדש כי ממשיכין לה החיות מן הקדושה מתחלת המחשבה עד סוף המעשה כנ"ל. ואזי התבואה נתקדשה בקדושת שלימות לה"ק שהוא בחי' פי שנים שעל ידו נברא העולם וכל אשר בה. וע"כ מפרישין אח"כ מעשר שני זה בחי' שלימות לה"ק ע"י תרגום. כי המעשר שני הוא בבחי' תרגום שהוא סמוך אל הקדושה ונאכל לזרים. והוא ממוצע בין מתנות הכונה שהם קודש לגמרי. ובין שאר התבואה הנאכלת לזרים. ועיקר מצותו הוא רק להעלותו לירושלים עיר הקודש. שהיא בחי' מלכות פה בחי' לשון הקודש ולאוכלו שם. שעי"ז עולה הטוב שבתרגום ללה"ק והרע נכנע ואזי הותרה התבואה באכילה לישראל. כי נכנע הרעעל ידי בחי' שלימות לה"ק ע"י התרגום כנ"ל. ע' לעיל בה' ערלה (הלכה א') שם מבואר קצת יותר בחי' מעשר שני. כי הוא בחי' נטע רבעי שהוא בחי' לשון תרגום המשלים לשון הקודש על ידי שנאכל בירושלים כנ"ל:
segments.en: And this is the aspect of “and G-d separated between the light and the darkness” (Beraishis 1:4) — which are the aspects of raishis and shirayim. For the light is in the East, which is called kedem [before/east], the aspect of raishis; and the darkness, which is the setting of the light, is in the West, which is called achor v'sof [behind and end], the aspect of shirayim. And when there is separation between the light and the darkness, between the raishis and the shirayim — then is the essential rectification of the world, that the shirayim too are rectified through the raishis, in the aspect of “v'nish'ar gam hu le'Elokaynu” as mentioned. And this is: “and there was evening and there was morning, day one” (Beraishis 1:5) — that the evening and the morning are included together, which are the raishis and the shirayim, and both are included in the unity of the world in the aspect of “nish'ar gam hu” etc. — which is the aspect of “day one” (yom echad), said because Hashem blessed-be-He was alone (yachid) in His world (Rashi, ad loc.). For specifically through Hashem blessed-be-He separating between the light and the darkness — that is, between the raishis and the shirayim — and one knows who is the raishis and who is the shirayim: then specifically the shirayim too are rectified and included in Hashem blessed-be-He, in the aspect of “v'nish'ar gam hu le'Elokaynu,” the aspect of “and there was evening and there was morning, day one” as mentioned. And this is the secret of Havdalah (sod haHavdalah) — that specifically through making Havdalah and saying “HaMavdil bain kodesh l'chol” [Who separates between the holy and the mundane], specifically through this the weekdays too are sanctified, and the holiness of Shabbos is drawn upon them, and the grip of the serpent's defilement (zuhamas hanachash) is expelled from the weekdays — as is known, for this is the essential secret of Havdalah. And on the face of it this seems the opposite — for are we not making separation between the holiness of Shabbos and the weekdays? So how are the weekdays sanctified through this? But it is as mentioned: for specifically through the Havdalah by which one separates between the holy and the mundane, between the seventh day and the six days of labor, and one knows and reveals that the essential holiness and the essential sustenance of the world is Shabbos, and all the weekdays are the aspect of shirayim which were all created only for the sake of Shabbos — specifically through this the weekdays too are sanctified with the holiness of Shabbos. Through the fact that they toil throughout all the weekdays for the sake of Shabbos — this being their essential elevation and rectification — as it is written: “Remember the day of Shabbos” — remember it from the first day of the week (Mechilta, Shemos 20:8) etc. And through this the six weekdays are included in the holiness of Shabbos and are sanctified from the serpent's defilement. For as long as one does not make separation between the holiness of Shabbos and the weekdays, and does not reveal the difference, it appears heaven forbid as though all faces are equal and one does not know who is the raishis and who is the shirayim — then the world is in the aspect of tohu vavohu and darkness etc. But specifically through Havdalah, which reveals the greatness of the holiness of Shabbos as the essential thing and the raishis — the aspect of “the first among the holy convocations” (techillah l'mikra'ei kodesh) (Vayikra 23:2 — as the Sages expounded of Shabbos) — specifically through this the shirayim, which are the weekdays, are also sanctified. For this is the essential rectification of the world and its fullness, which was created for this, for the sake of the raishis as mentioned — that is, that the whole world was created for the sake of Israel and the Torah, so that all would toil and labor for the sake of Israel and the Torah who are the essential thing and the raishis. And likewise among Israel themselves: the masses and the amay ha'aretz [common people] must toil and labor to support the talmiday chachamim [Torah scholars] and the G-d-fearing who occupy themselves with His service blessed-be-He, for they are the essential raishis. And likewise throughout all the weekdays one must toil for the sake of the holiness of Shabbos as mentioned. And then specifically, when one knows who is the raishis and who is the shirayim, and the shirayim toil for the sake of the raishis — then the shirayim too are sanctified and included in the raishis, in the aspect of “v'nish'ar gam hu le'Elokaynu” as mentioned. And therefore in the commandment of Chalah there must be specifically raishis and shirayim, as it is written: “raishis,” that its remainder (shirayim) be recognizable — for this is the essential wholeness and rectification, that the shirayim be rectified through the raishis as mentioned. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory expounded the verse Beraishis upon Bikkurim, Terumah, and Chalah — which are called raishis — that for their sake the world was created. For it is all one: for all the commandments of Chalah, Terumah, and Bikkurim are all in the aforementioned aspect — to sanctify and to separate the raishis, so that through this the shirayim too are clarified and rectified. And this itself is the whole of Creation: that the whole world and its fullness — which is the aspect of shirayim — was created for the sake of the raishis, which is Israel and the Torah as mentioned. For it is all one as mentioned. And this is: “If there is no flour, there is no Torah” (im ein kemach ein Torah) (Avos 3:17). The words of Torah are compared to a millstone (rechayim), as our Sages of blessed memory said: just as the millstone never ceases etc. (Midrash). For the clarification (berur) of the flour from which bread is made is like the clarification of Torah — which requires precise examination (dikduk) and thorough grinding until the halachah is clarified in its truth. And then one merits the nahama d'Orayta [bread of Torah], the aspect of “come, eat of my bread” (l'chu lachamu b'lachmi) (Mishlay 9:5). And this itself is the clarification of the flour: one must grind the wheat into flour so that the sparks are divided very, very finely — in the aspect of the ketores [incense] of which it is said “and you shall grind some of it very fine” (v'shachakta mimena hadek) (Shemos 30:36), and when one grinds it one says: “grind it fine, fine, grind it” (hadek haytiv haytiv hadek). And on Yom Kippur, when one must clarify and raise from the deepest depths of the klippos more and more — for then all sins are atoned — therefore then the ketores must be dakah min hadakah [fine beyond fine]. For this is the general rule: the more that sparks require rectification and clarification, the more they need to be divided into ever more parts — as is explained in Sefer HaGilgulim [Book of Transmigrations]. And this is the aspect of flour: it is impossible to make bread unless one first grinds the wheat into flour, which is ground and divided into very, very fine particles — so that the sparks are divided into very many parts, so that we can then specifically gather them and clarify them and make from them dough and bread. Then they are included in the stature of man (komat adam) through the man eating them — and they are the essential vitality and satisfaction of man: namely the sparks which are the divine vitality (chiyus Elokyus) within them, from which comes the essential satisfaction and life-force. And this is what Rashi explained regarding the creation of the first Adam: “he kneaded the dough” (lash es ha'isah) (Sanhedrin 38b) — for it is all one. For the dust of the first Adam was gathered from all parts of the world, for all the sparks and all the souls were included in him — as is known. And this is the aspect of dough (isah) made from flour as mentioned — which is the aspect of Torah, the aspect of “if there is no flour, there is no Torah.” And this is why the clarification of the halachos by talmiday chachamim was compared to the clarification of foods — as the Mishnah says: “there are four types among students: a sponge, a funnel, a strainer, and a sieve” (sefog, mashpech, mishemeres, nafah) (Avos 5:15). And therefore the essential completion of the clarification is through the Chalah separated from the dough made of flour and water — the waters of da'as [knowledge] and Torah drawn upon the flour. And through this one gathers and collects it and kneads it and makes dough. And then it is obligated in Chalah: to give the raishis to the Kohen who is composed of ben v'talmid, through which the entire dough is included in the aforementioned aspect, in the aspect of Torah and da'as, through which all the sparks ascend etc. as mentioned. And therefore Chalah is practiced even now outside the Land of Israel, because through Chalah comes the essential clarification as mentioned. And this is why the Torah portion of Chalah is juxtaposed with the Torah portion of the Spies (Meraglim) in the portion Shelach Lecha (Bamidbar 13–15). For the Spies blemished the Land of Israel and blemished the aspect of the illumination of ben v'talmid — as is understood from the aforementioned Torah. For they passed through the Land of Israel when it was still in exile under the hand of the seven nations. And when they came there they were seized with fears, and they were placed there in a state of smallness and lowliness (katnus v'shiplut), in the aspect of exile, as it is written: “and we were in our own eyes as grasshoppers” (vanhi v'ainaynu kachagavim) etc. (Bamidbar 13:33). But they ought to have strengthened themselves to believe in Hashem and in Moshe His servant, that through his great power He would conquer everything before them, and everything would be returned to Hashem blessed-be-He and to Israel — as indeed happened afterward in truth. But they denied this. And therefore it was decreed upon them weeping for generations, that Israel must linger so long in exile. And through the fact that there are even now tzaddikim who strengthen us to believe in Hashem blessed-be-He that He will conquer everything before us, and everything will ascend to Hashem blessed-be-He in the aspect of “v'nish'ar gam hu le'Elokaynu” — through this we rectify the sin of the Spies who blemished this. And through this Mashiach Tzidkaynu will come and redeem us speedily, and everything will return to Hashem blessed-be-He as mentioned. And this is the aspect of Chalah to the Kohen, which is the aspect of “v'nish'ar gam hu le'Elokaynu.” And therefore the portion of Chalah is juxtaposed in the portion of Shelach Lecha as mentioned. And this is also the aspect of the portion of Minchas Nesachim [flour-offerings and libations] (Bamidbar 15:1–16) which is juxtaposed immediately with the portion of the Spies, and then right afterward the portion of Chalah. For menachos [flour-offerings] are brought from flour, where the essential clarification resides — which is the aspect of Chalah as mentioned. And therefore the essential drawing close of Israel to Hashem blessed-be-He at the Exodus from Egypt and the Receiving of the Torah was through the flour-offering of the Omer on Pesach and the Shtay HaLechem [Two Loaves] on Shavuos. For menachos and Chalah which come from flour — which are the rectification of bread, which is the essential food — there is the illumination of the Will which is the essential rectification, drawn through the illumination of ben v'talmid. Which is the essential da'as [knowledge] to know Hashem, which is drawn on Pesach and Shavuos. And therefore it is juxtaposed with the portion of the Spies who blemished all of this. For through menachos and Chalah, which are the rectification of bread, through which one merits the illumination of the Will etc. — through this the blemish of the Spies is rectified. For through this we will merit to go out from exile, and all the sparks will be clarified and ascend, and speedily it will be fulfilled: “v'nish'ar gam hu le'Elokaynu” etc. as mentioned. Speedily in our days, Amen.
